name: Croatia
summary: Children, a spouse and partners are guaranteed half of their intestate share, and dependent parents a third. A foreign resident can choose the law of their nationality (EU Succession Regulation art. 22). Croatia has no trusts, and foundations are for public benefit only.
reserved_share: Descendants, adopted children, spouse and registered or informal partners: half of their intestate share. Parents and other ancestors: one third of the intestate share, only if permanently unable to work and without means (Succession Act, Zakon o nasljeđivanju). A forced heir can be excluded only on grounds the will states.
foreign_law_note: EU Succession Regulation: the law of the last habitual residence applies by default (art. 21), but a resident foreign national may choose the law of their nationality (art. 22).
trust_note: Croatia is not in the HCCH table for the 1985 Trusts Convention. Croatian law has no trust. Foundations (zaklade) are governed by the Foundations Act, NN 106/18, 98/19, 151/22, and serve a public-benefit or charitable purpose.
open_questions: Succession Act article numbers not captured (e-Justice cites none).
Foundation purposes taken from search snippets, not the statute text.
